string.text: AnimusForge Xihai Action loaded (v1.1 / Framework V4 + Battle Speech V2).
AnimusForge Xihai Action disabled: the required AnimusForge runtime contract is unavailable.
Battle speech did not start: no eligible allied soldiers were found.
Battle speech is available only while deployment or an active battle is continuing.
Battle speech did not start: the selected speaker is unavailable.
Battle speech did not start: other-speaker speech requires a selected allied soldier.
Battle speech did not start: the selected speaker is attacking or preparing an attack.
Battle speech did not start: an enemy is too close to the speaker.

Recognizes natural action wording in player shouts and NPC replies, uses AF closed-set fallback for complex wording, and recognizes natural battle-speech requests and speech gestures. Disable it to stop these natural-language paths.
AF speech action and audience-reply analysis
Enable battle-speech recognition from T-key scene shout
When enabled, T-key scene-shout text can enter the battle-speech channel. Y-key speech entries still require the main battle-speech switch and an eligible battle phase.
Move NPC to the front line
Maximum spoken replies submitted per tick
Hard Mission-tick budget for spoken soldier reply bridge calls; independent from the logical wave size.
Command gesture then order all formations to Advance
When an enemy enters this radius, the speech continues in place. Soldiers may show written replies, but speaker/audience actions, native battle cries, command gestures, and Advance are suppressed.
Master switch for battle speech. Disabling it hides T-key routing, speech length, staging, audience response, and post-speech order options.
Minimum AF-generated battle-speech body length. Generation and display share the same frozen snapshot. Must not exceed the maximum.
Maximum AF-generated battle-speech body length. Results beyond this limit are rejected fail-closed.
Moves an NPC speaker in front of the friendly line and turns them toward the soldiers. Disabling keeps the speaker in place and takes no scripted movement control.
Distance the NPC moves forward from the friendly line center. Used only while speaker staging is enabled.
The NPC is considered in position inside this radius. This affects only staging arrival detection.
Maximum staging wait. On timeout the NPC safely speaks from the current position; no teleport and no duplicate request.
Includes same-side allies in the frozen audience. Allies may respond but never receive the player's post-speech Advance order.
Maximum soldiers sampled for controlled response actions. Sampling is deterministic and submissions are batched to avoid full-army frame synchronization.
Soldier actions in one logical wave. This is a wave size, not the per-Mission-tick bridge-call budget.
Maximum action bridge calls submitted per Mission tick. Limits frame load independently from the logical wave size.
Plays native battle cries in batches during audience response without AF TTS. Disabling hides battle-cry count, wave, and interval options.
Maximum soldiers using native battle cries in this speech. Affects sound scale and performance only.
Native battle cries triggered together in one wave. Smaller waves sound less synchronized and spread the performance load.
Delay between native battle-cry waves. Does not change the random interval for written soldier replies.
Lets multiple soldiers answer the speech with short lines. Disabling hides reply count, waves, length, and interval options.
Maximum soldiers generating written replies for this speech. Each selected soldier is submitted only once.
Maximum written replies in one logical wave. Independent from the per-Mission-tick submission budget.
Minimum length of each soldier reply. Does not affect the battle-speech body.
Maximum length of each soldier reply. Keep replies short to reduce reading and performance pressure when many soldiers answer.
Lower bound of the random delay between written-reply waves. Works with the per-tick budget to limit request spikes.
Upper bound of the random delay between written-reply waves. Must not be below the minimum interval.
After the speech and audience response, the speaker performs a command gesture and orders the player's formations to Advance. Allies respond but are not ordered.
Delay between the command gesture and Advance orders to the player's formations. Used only while post-speech Advance is enabled.
Shows battle-speech start, cancellation, and completion notices. Disabling affects UI only, not execution.
Writes detailed natural-action and battle-speech diagnostics. Disabling reduces log I/O without changing behavior.
